## 1601 N Milwaukee Ave — Zoning & Development Analysis
**PIN:** 14313320180000 | West Town (Community Area 24) | Ward 32

---

### 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **B3-2** (Community Shopping District, bulk density designation 2), per the City's official GIS parcel record (Ordinance No. 17230). Verify at the [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning).

---

### 2. Ground-Floor Retail with Apartments Above

**Yes — this is a permitted use in B3.** The B3 district accommodates a broad range of retail and service uses [1], and [1] explicitly states that residential dwelling units are permitted **above the ground floor** [1]. Ground-floor retail with apartments above is a classic B3 configuration and does not require a special entitlement in this district.

---

### 3. Key Bulk & Density Standards

The retrieved code text does not include the specific FAR table, height table, or minimum lot-area-per-unit table for B3-2 (those appear in unretrieved subsections of § 17-3-0403-A and § 17-3-0402). What the code does confirm:

- **FAR:** B3 districts are subject to maximum FAR standards set in [3] (§ 17-3-0403-A). The B3-2 dash designation (−2) sets the specific number, but the table itself was not in the retrieved text. An **FAR increase** for transit-served locations is available only in **B-3 and C-3 districts** (i.e., dash-3 districts such as B3-3), not B3-2 — so no FAR bonus applies here by right [3].
- **Minimum Lot Area per Unit:** Standard B3-2 minimums apply per § 17-3-0402. The MLA reduction for transit-served locations requires a Type 1 Map Amendment or Planned Development and is available only in **D-3 districts** per [2], not B3-2.
- **Setbacks:** Not in the retrieved text for this district. Verify in § 17-3-0500 and the zoning map.
- **Stories/Height:** Not retrieved. Check § 17-3-0403 and the B3-2 row of Table 17-3-0403-A.

**How to verify:** Contact the Department of Planning & Development (DPD) or use the [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning) to pull the full bulk standards table, or request a Zoning Certificate of Use.

---

### 4. Overlays and Special Designations

This parcel carries a significant stack of overlays:

- **Milwaukee Avenue Historic District** — This parcel is within a Chicago Historic District (layer: `historic_district`). Exterior alterations will likely require review; contact the Commission on Chicago Landmarks.
- **Individual Landmark Building** — The parcel is flagged as an **individual Chicago landmark** (is_landmark_building: true). The Chicago Historic Resources Survey rates it **"orange"** (historically significant building, surveyed as "Noel State Bank"). Landmark status imposes strict controls on demolition and exterior alteration, enforced by the Commission on Chicago Landmarks.
- **Wicker Park Historic District (National Register)** — Also listed on the **National Register of Historic Places** [data:business]. This does not by itself prevent demolition under local law, but it enables **Federal Historic Tax Credits** for qualifying rehabilitations.
- **Transit-Oriented Development — CTA** — The parcel is within a CTA TOD area (0.07 miles from Damen Blue Line) [4]. Parking minimums may be reduced up to 100% per § 17-10-0102-B (see §5 below). No density/FAR/height bonus applies at B3-2 (only dash-3 districts qualify) [3].
- **ADU Eligible Area** — Accessory Dwelling Units (coach houses, etc.) may be established here per § 17-9-0201-F [5], subject to the rear-30-feet rule and 22-foot height limit [5].
- **Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone** — Any residential development triggering an entitlement (zoning change, PD, etc.) will be subject to ARO affordable unit requirements. The West Town community area already has 20 ARO projects totaling 291 affordable units.
- **Wicker Park Special Service Area (SSA)** — An SSA levy applies to properties here. The tax breakdown confirms a **City of Chicago Special Service Area 33** levy of ~$2,363/year at current assessment.
- **No Planned Development** — This parcel is not in a Planned Development.
- **No Lakefront Protection, no PMD, no special district.**

---

### 5. Parking Requirement & Transit Reduction

Because this parcel is within 2,640 feet of a CTA rail station entrance (Damen Blue Line, 0.07 miles), it qualifies as a transit-served location under [4]. Per § 17-10-0102-B, the **minimum parking requirement may be reduced by up to 100%** — meaning zero off-street parking can be required for a qualifying project [4]. This reduction is **by right** at B3-2 (no additional entitlement required for the parking relief itself). Note that new construction in transit-served B/C districts must also comply with pedestrian-street design criteria of § 17-3-0308 [4].

---

### 6. Demolition & New Mixed-Use Construction

**Possible, but heavily constrained by landmark status.** Key considerations:

- **Individual Landmark — Demolition Review Required:** Because this building is designated an **individual Chicago landmark** (Noel State Bank), demolition requires approval from the **Commission on Chicago Landmarks** and City Council. This is a high bar — landmark demolition is rarely approved outright.
- **Historic District Exterior Controls:** Even short of demolition, the Milwaukee Avenue Historic District overlay means exterior work requires landmark commission review.
- **National Register:** Federal historic tax credits are available for a certified rehabilitation — demolition would forfeit these.
- **New Construction Criteria:** Any new construction within 2,640 feet of a CTA rail station must satisfy § 17-3-0308 criteria [4], including compliance with parking standards (§ 17-10-0102-B) and pedestrian-street design standards (§ 17-3-0504).
- **Wrecking Permit:** The area has had 57 demolition permits issued recently [data:permits], but a standard wrecking permit cannot be issued for a landmark without Commission approval.
- **ARO Trigger:** If a zoning entitlement is sought (e.g., map amendment to increase density), ARO affordable unit obligations are triggered [3].
- **Brownfield Proximity:** A brownfield site (Park 512 Avenue Park, EPA ID 110005863100) is nearby — environmental due diligence is advisable before any ground disturbance.
- **No FAR or density bonus** is available at B3-2 by right. A project requiring greater density would need a Type 1 Map Amendment or Planned Development per [3].

**Realistic path:** Adaptive reuse/rehabilitation of the existing landmark building is far more feasible than demolition. A certified historic rehabilitation could combine Federal Historic Tax Credits with the ARO-zone mixed-use program and zero-parking TOD relief.
